Axiom:
**Default: minimum coherent tickets — one per module-spec or independently verifiable infrastructure capability.** Prefer keeping related work together over speculative fragmentation. Uncertain dependencies favor keeping work together, not guessed DAG edges. Use phases for internal implementation order.
DAG edges derive from real file-level dependencies, Bootstrap → consumers, and cross-scope `depends-on`. No «logical layer» phases — Ports → Adapters → Integrations is an analysis aid in discovery, NOT a ticket-multiplication rule. A Port and its single confirmed-v1 Adapter co-edit and live in one ticket.
A split needs an evidence-backed boundary and a concrete benefit over keeping one ticket: independently verifiable outcomes, a demonstrated phase-context limit, or safe useful parallelism. File count, desired ticket count and imagined parallelism are not evidence. A large file or many phases alone do not establish a context limit. A necessary sequential split names the exact producer/consumer artifact and why phases in one ticket are insufficient.
Parallel dispatch additionally requires disjoint Target Files across all phases, no dependency relation, and no hidden shared writer or prerequisite. Keep dependency order topological and acyclic; preserve Bootstrap → consumers and cross-scope dependencies. Independent outputs must still cover the complete user outcome together.
**NOT a reason to split:** audit milestone granularity (audit runs once per GROUP — every ticket of the spec, together, per `AX_AUDIT_HOOK` — regardless of ticket size or count, never once per ticket); logical layering (Port + Adapter ship together); partial shippability (consumer can't pick a half-module); human time-units (hours / days — irrelevant for AI execution bounded by context window).
A sequential split with a hard dependency earns no parallel speedup. It needs a demonstrated context or independently verifiable outcome boundary that phases in one ticket cannot serve; otherwise the extra handoff and repeated reading are overhead.
Cross-scope: scope B DONE before A's tasks consuming B's outputs. Bootstrap tickets DONE before non-bootstrap of the same scope.
